input.quote: Licenses. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, RevMed hereby grants to Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), royalty-bearing license (which shall be sub-licensable solely as provided in Section 3.4) under the RevMed Licensed Technology, to Research, Develop, Manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise Commercialize and exploit Products (including, for clarity, any Companion Diagnostics with respect to such Products) in the Field in the Licensed Territory.
input.rationale: The grant to us (Section 3.1(a), p0248) is exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), covers the full value chain in the "Field" (defined as "any and all uses") and the "Licensed Territory" (all countries and territories of the world), and is not revocable at RevMed's discretion — RevMed can terminate only for uncured material breach (p0491), insolvency (p0492) or the negotiated Competing Product / cessation-of-activity triggers (p0493, p0495), each with notice and cure. Affiliate and contractor coverage sits at the preferred position: Section 3.4(a) lets us exercise rights and perform obligations through any Affiliate without RevMed's consent, Section 3.4(b) permits sublicensing through multiple tiers (only a U.S. "substantially all" sublicense needs consent that cannot be unreasonably withheld), and Section 3.4(c)(i) lets us subcontract to Third Parties as we deem appropriate. Section 15.2(a)(ii) permits assignment without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all related assets, merger or acquisition, satisfying the transferability requirement. Only drafting nuance: Affiliate/contractor rights live in Section 3.4 rather than in the grant language itself, and the U.S. mega-sublicense consent and Acquiror-Family carve-outs (p0612) are mild frictions — noted, not material deviations.
